rows: Quote me exactly. Then tell me where my claim goes wrong.
Brawling is not a verdict on anything. Show me what the brawl was meant to prove.
A risk is a debt you take on. Know the amount before you sign for it.
You want to slow the match. Say so in those words, so I can hold you to them.
The people are owed a plain account. I will give them one, word for word.
In one sentence you say you are ready. I say you have not shown it yet.
You describe yourself as central. Show me the document that puts you there.
Look at the stance. It says nothing you have not already said with your feet.
You claim technical skill. Quote the hold, name what it requires, and I will judge it.
A brawl without a verdict is only noise. Give me a result I can check.
Risk is an exposure. You have not shown me the size of yours.
A stall breaks what you promised. I will quote the promise back to you.
The crowd is owed a result they can rely on. Tell them what you will deliver.
You have called yourself one of the best. Which exact moment supports the word?
You are proud of your {strength}. Quote the part you rely on, and I will answer that part only.
I have checked your {strength} against what you said before. They do not match.
A calm answer. Good. Calm is the easiest state in which to be held to your words.
You have said it precisely. I will hold you to it precisely.
I could challenge the whole sentence. I will challenge the single word that matters.
One fall. Keep me down, and the verdict is yours, in the exact words we used.
On the mat, I will quote you as we go. Stay with what you said.
Grounded or standing, your promise is the same promise. Keep it.
Stay in front of me. Repeat your claim so I can take it down correctly.
A sound answer. It matches what you said earlier, word for word.
You have not answered. A promise left unanswered is still owed.
I accept that for the moment. We will settle the debt at the bell.
I will wrestle this match and hold you to every word you have given.
My approach is exact. I say a thing once, and I mean it.
Whatever happens, the words will be on the table in the order you said them.
The verdict is not in. One promise still stands open.
I have one more quotation for you, and you will hear it when the bell rings.
